title: GLMZ Stories: Vol. 1
premise: Three stand-alone chapters from the unsorted edges of the city — a neuro-integration specialist counting eleven seconds of silence in a ward at 0247, a barber on his thirty-second year of the same morning ritual, and a tamale-buyer who learns the road home is a road that no longer exists. No shared protagonist. No shared arc. The city is the through-line, and the city does not need an arc to be felt.
arc_target: GLMZ in the small register — the hospital ward, the barbershop, the cold tamale on a counter — where the world's larger violence is felt as a quiet displacement of small certainties. An anthology, deliberately. The reader leaves with a feeling rather than a conclusion.
tagline: Three rooms. Three lives. One city that doesn't notice.
